text:
ariane: FYI rolling FP8 kernel to L40S canary flagged a weird regression on a handful of models. Seeing sudden NaNs and token-level quality shifts on span-extraction tests. :eyes:

kenji: which models / commit? any logs yet?

ariane: canary id 2026-03-12.fp8-l40s-01 (deployed ~1894567800). Failing on xgen-7b and a custom summarizer. CI logs show matmul NaN in attention layers. small repro attached below.

samir: can you paste the minimal repro? I can try to bisect config vs kernel.

ariane: reproducer (run on L40S with our inference image):
```bash
python - <<'PY'
from redwood import InferenceClient
cli = InferenceClient(model='xgen-7b', device='l40s', runtime_opts={'enable_fp8': True, 'mix_precision': 'fp8-fp16'})
print(cli.generate('Extract the answer: Why does the cat purr?\n', max_tokens=64))
PY
```

ariane: log excerpt: 
```
E 03:12:04 kernel.cpp:457 matmul kernel threw: NaN detected in output
E 03:12:04 layer17/attn: activation range overflow: max=1.2e38
```

kenji: Hmm that activation range is wild. We've seen overflow from scale mismatch when using per-channel scaling vs global scaling for activations. Which FP8 profile are you using?

ariane: Using fp8-profile v2 (auto-scale per-tensor), default compiler picks wp8-tile-32.

samir: quick experiment: try forcing activation-scaling="layerwise" and disable continuous batching + kvprefetch. I've seen batching amplify small numerical noise into large overflows.

ariane: tried that: set runtime_opts {'activation_scaling': 'layerwise', 'continuous_batching': False, 'kv_prefetch': False} — still get NaN but only on long context > 1024 tokens. Shorter contexts ok.

eva: re: long context — could be KV tile stride mismatch between H100-optimized kernel and L40S fallback kernels. We had a tiling bug where leftover tail tokens used an uninitialized scratch buffer.

samir: can you run with env REDWOOD_DEBUG_TILING=1 and attach the kernel tiling dump? Also try forcing kernel "h100-tiling-compat" fallback on L40S to see if behavior changes.

ariane: dump attached in CI: https://ci.redwood.dev/job/1894/tiling-dump.txt (excerpt below)
```
TILE: layer17: tile_size=64 tail=12 use_fast_path=1
ALLOC scratch=0x7fffaabbcc00 size=4096 (not zeroed)
```

ci-deploy-bot: Canary 2026-03-12.fp8-l40s-01: health degraded -> rollback scheduled (reason: kernel NaN). :warning:

kenji: OK that's useful. If scratch buffer isn't zeroed on tail path, tiny numerical garbage could scale into FP8's narrow dynamic range and saturate. Two paths: (1) ensure zero-init of scratch on tail path, (2) change activation rescale to include clamp before quantization.

samir: I bisected to a kernel change in commit 0xbee7a3 where we introduced a tail-path fast-path optimization to avoid memzero for perf. Reproducer passes if I revert that commit.

ariane: great catch. Perf win is small (<1.8%) but correctness > perf. Recommend revert and add explicit zeroing guarded by an env flag to avoid silent regressions.

eva: also add a small numeric test to our canary suite: run long-context sampling with fp8 enabled and check for finite outputs + per-layer activation mins/maxes. Make it run on both H100 and L40S.

kenji: Agreed. I'll open a PR: revert tail-path nonzero optimization, add memzero + test + a new env REDWOOD_FP8_ALLOW_UNINITIALIZED=0 (default).

ariane: for bookkeeping: observed quality deltas on our micro-eval set when kernel was enabled on L40S: exact-match 0.842 -> 0.768, ppl 12.3 -> 18.7, token-level entropy up ~15%. INT8/GPTQ runs unaffected.

samir: thanks — those numbers make the decision trivial. Tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre to watch canary rollbacks.

eva: postmortem action items: (1) revert commit 0xbee7a3, (2) add tile-zero meminit on tail path, (3) add long-context fp8 smoke to canary, (4) update docs about mixed-precision pitfalls (activation scaling & tail-tiling).

ariane: I'll follow-up with a short incident note and link to the PR once I'm back at my desk. :thumbsup:
